description: DEMO CONFIG. Every block below is annotated so the repo doubles as documentation.
config:recommended    - Renovate's maintained baseline preset. Dependabot has no preset system at all.
:dependencyDashboard  - opens ONE tracking issue listing every pending/rate-limited/errored update,
with checkboxes that create the PR on demand. Dependabot has no equivalent.
group:monorepos       - auto-groups packages published from the same monorepo (e.g. @typescript-eslint/*)
from a community-maintained list. Zero per-package config.
Security updates bypass the normal schedule and jump the queue.
osvVulnerabilityAlerts:true (above) sources advisories from osv.dev directly,
so this works even where GitHub's alert pipeline is unavailable or disabled.
Weekly PR that regenerates package-lock.json from scratch, refreshing TRANSITIVE
dependencies that no manifest change would ever touch. Dependabot has no counterpart:
it only bumps transitives when an advisory names them.

customManagers.description: Update `ARG <TOOL>_VERSION=` lines in the Dockerfile using inline `# renovate:` annotations. No built-in manager - and no Dependabot feature - can do this.

packageRules.description: LANE 1 - devDependency non-major. One PR per week, automerged once CI is green. You are never meant to look at this PR.
LANE 2 - production non-major. One reviewable PR per week, one CI run.
LANE 3 - non-npm managers have no depType, so Lanes 1-2 cannot match them. Without this rule Docker/Actions/regex updates stay as individual PRs. Most common grouping mistake.

LANE 4 - majors are the one thing you must NOT group. dependencyDashboardApproval keeps them silent until you tick their checkbox: quiet without losing isolation. Grouping majors is exactly what broke Dependabot PRs #3 and #5.
prPriority only - lifts runtime-critical packages up the queue. Deliberately last so it does not override lane labels or grouping.
